name: Gamzigrad-Romuliana, Palace of Galerius
description: Near the town of Zaječar in eastern Serbia, Felix Romuliana is a fortified Roman palace built around 300 AD by Emperor Galerius and named after his mother, Romula. Walls and towers enclose temples, baths, basilicas and imperial apartments. Just up the hill, a memorial complex was meant to honour the emperor and his mother after death, which makes this retirement residence unusually ceremonial.
